thread.title: What to watch: European chip makers hit by Apple, Next cuts guidance, and UK skills squeeze

author: uk.finance.yahoo.com
title: What to watch: European chip makers hit by Apple, Next cuts guidance, and UK skills squeeze
text: Surprisingly upbeat: Next beat city forecasts for Christmas sales but downgraded full-year profit forecasts. Photo: Matthew Horwood/Getty Images More Here are the top business, market, and economic stories you should be watching today in the UK, Europe, and abroad: European chip makers hit by Apple Shares in European-listed microchip suppliers fell on Thursday after Apple ( AAPL ) cut guidance overnight, stoking fears of a global slowdown in smartphone demand. Apple unexpectedly slashed its revenue forecast for the fiscal first quarter of 2019 late on Wednesday , citing weakness in its key market of China and lower-than-anticipated iPhone revenue. Shares in the tech giant fell over 8% on the announcement. Suppliers to Apple and other chip makers are now seeing share price declines as investors reason that a slowdown in iPhone sales could dent revenues of company’s in smartphone supply chains. Dialog Semiconductor ( DLG.DE ) was down 7%, STMicroelectronics ( STM.PA ) was down by 6%, BE Semiconductor ( BESI.AS ) was down 5%, and Austrian chipmaker AMS ( AMS.VI ) was down by 17%. READ MORE: Tim Cook blamed China for Apple weakness: Here’s what he said about the country in 2018 Next cuts guidance but surprises on sales High street retailer Next ( NXT.L ) cut forecasts for its full-year profits but confounded fears of a Christmas sales slowdown. Next said in a trading update on Thursday that full-price sales from the end of October to the start of December rose by 1.5%, which was in-line with its forecasts. Analysts had feared that the retailer would post a fall in sales. Next trimmed its pretax profit forecast for the year ahead from £727m to £723m. However, it upgraded its sales forecasts for 2019 from 3% to 3.2%. Shares in Next were up by 3%. READ MORE: Next lowers profit guidance but Christmas sales rise UK hit by skills squeeze British manufacturers are facing a skills shortage, according to a survey conducted by the British Chamber of Commerce (BCC). The business lobbying group said that 81% of manufacturing companies it surveyed reported problems recruiting staff, which is the joint highest level since the survey began in 1989. Some 70% of companies in the service sector, which accounts for around 80% of UK economic output, also reported trouble recruiting staff. The BCC ‘s survey of 6,000 firms found the economy is “stuck in a weak holding pattern, with stagnating levels of growth and business confidence as a result of heightened Brexit uncertainty and other economic pressures.” Companies could collapse in no-deal Brexit A range of British companies could simply collapse if the UK crashes out of the European Union in late March with no Brexit deal. No amount of forward planning would be able to save them. Experts have outlined a range of different types of companies that could be forced to close in the event of a no-deal Brexit, including food firms and small businesses that rely on large European customers. “You can only plan for so much,” Andrew Opie, a director at the British Retail Consortium, told Yahoo Finance UK. “Any company that is importing or exporting from the EU, our largest market, still doesn’t know how the system is going to work if there’s a no-deal Brexit.” READ MORE: These UK companies could collapse in a no-deal Brexit European markets European stock markets were lower as global investors dumped riskier assets following Apple’s revenue warning. Britain’s FTSE 100 ( ^FTSE ) was down by 0.1%, Germany’s DAX ( ^GDAXI ) was down by 0.5%, France’s CAC 40 ( ^FCHI ) was down by 0.5%, and the Euronext 100 ( ^N100 ) was 0.6% lower. Asian markets were lower too. Japan’s Nikkei 225 ( ^N225 ) closed down by 0.3%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index ( ^HSI ) was down by 0.2%, and China’s benchmark Shanghai Composite ( 1.SS ) was 0.03% lower. READ MORE: Apple bombshell rocks European, Asian shares; ‘flash crash’ jolts currencies What to expect in the US US stock futures were pointing to a sharply lower open. S&P 500 futures ( ES=F ) were down by 1.3%, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures ( YM=F ) were 1.2% lower, and Nasdaq futures ( NQ=F ) were down by 2.5%.
